title: Bounded-below exceptional pullback over a quasi-compact target
statement: Let X and Y be schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], f : X → Y a morphism admitting a compactification, Y quasi-compact, and Λ a finite commutative ring. For the chosen ordinary étale lower shriek on unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], Rf_! is a left adjoint and its chosen right adjoint Rf^! preserves globally bounded-below objects. This is the proposition HasBoundedBelowUpperShriek (ModuleCat Λ) f. The quasi-compactness hypothesis is essential.

source.place: lemma-proper-mod-n-direct-sums and lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper; morphisms.tex lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension; derived.tex Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived (4)(c); SGA 4 XVIII 3.1.7 adjunction argument

proof.text: Take the chosen compactification X → Z → Y, with proper map g. The finite-type fibre-dimension bound supplies d with all fibres of g of dimension ≤ d, since Y is quasi-compact. Base extension of a finite-type scheme over a field preserves its dimension, so every geometric fibre also has dimension ≤ d.

For a sheaf G and q>2d, proper base change identifies the geometric-point pullback of R^q g_* G with the higher direct image of its restriction to the geometric fibre. Apply the relative torsion direct-image dimension bound to this proper scheme over the algebraic closure of the residue field. The resulting sheaf is zero. Geometric points detect zero sheaves, so R^q g_* G=0 globally, uniformly in G.

The upper-amplitude theorem for unbounded derived functors now puts Rg_* L in D^(≤ n+2d) whenever L lies in D^(≤n). Exact extension by zero preserves D^(≤n), so the chosen Rf_! = D(i_!) ⋙ Rg_* has the same upper-amplitude bound.

Finite coefficients give the ordinary left-adjoint instance. Apply the already proved amplitude-to-adjoint theorem with N=2d. Orthogonality and adjunction put Rf^! K in D^(≥ n-2d) whenever K lies in D^(≥n). This supplies the bounded-below instance without changing its statement.
